proposal: The Mandate recommends that the State Department's foreign assistance office (F), led by the USAID Administrator at Deputy Secretary rank, refocus most staff from preparing the annual budget proposal to executing appropriated money. It calls for dropping the duplicative Mission and Bureau Resource Requests, delivering the section 653(a) Foreign Assistance Act report to Congress within 60 days, fast-tracking congressional notifications and other pre-obligation steps, and publishing all notifications and reports.

status_summary: No source found shows the Mandate's process changes for the foreign assistance office: no end to the Mission and Bureau Resource Requests, no 60-day section 653(a) report, no fast-track for congressional notifications and no policy of publishing all notifications and reports. In the successor structure USAID no longer exists (its remaining operations merged into State on 2025-07-01), so there is no USAID-led F office; State Delegation of Authority No. 597 (published 2025-09-05) placed the Director of Foreign Assistance's powers under an Under Secretary, and the FY2026 explanatory statement makes enacted amounts available regardless of when the 653(a) report is sent. On timing of funds, GAO reported on 2026-09-30 that State announced a pause of all new obligations on 2025-01-24 pending review and lacked documented standards for aid decisions, and a special message of 2025-08-28 proposed rescinding nearly 5 billion dollars of foreign aid funds with fewer than 45 days left before they expired, which the Supreme Court let stand on an interim basis on 2025-09-26. These steps slowed rather than sped the availability of funds, but they concern whether funds are spent rather than the budget and notification process the text addresses, so the record stays at not_started rather than diverged.

timeline.event: NPR reported that one official served as USAID Deputy Administrator and State Director of Foreign Assistance and that his signature appeared on orders cancelling about 5,200 programs.
USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department, ending the agency that the Mandate would have placed in charge of the F office.

A special message proposed rescinding nearly 5 billion dollars of foreign assistance funds; according to CRS (Legal Sidebar of 2025-09-25), OMB then reapportioned the funds so they were unavailable for obligation, with fewer than 45 days left before they expired.

State published Delegation of Authority No. 597, placing the Director of Foreign Assistance's powers and those of five other aid-related offices under an Under Secretary for Foreign Assistance, Humanitarian Affairs, and Religious Freedom.

The Supreme Court granted a stay, pending appeal, of a district court order requiring obligation of expiring foreign aid funds, as to the funds covered by the 2025-08-28 special message; the order states it is not a final ruling on the merits.

title: Shift State's aid office from budget formulation to executing funds, speed notifications
uncertainties: Searches for the FY2025 and FY2026 section 653(a) reports (CRS, GAO, appropriators, one further web search in review) found no transmittal dates, so their timing is unknown; a Federal Register search for section 653(a) returned nothing relevant. The FY2026 explanatory statement says its funding tables are the basis for the 653(a) report and that amounts are available regardless of when the report is transmitted; the statement itself carries no date and its header labels the act Division B of a January 2026 minibus, so its source date (2026-01-11) is taken from the file name of the House-posted copy, and the act was enacted as Division F of Public Law 119-75 on 2026-02-03 per the GovInfo table of contents. The public posting requirement (reports posted within 45 days, section 7016(b) as described in the explanatory statement) is a congressional requirement, not an executive choice. The GAO 2019 report documents late 653(a) reports before 2025 and is background only. The GAO 2026 report does not mention the 653(a) report or an F bureau. The status of the Mission and Bureau Resource Request process and of public posting of notifications is unknown. The NPR article page shows no date; the date comes from its address. The withheld-funds evidence (special message, Supreme Court interim order, GAO pause finding) is context: it shows funds slowed, which some readers may judge as diverged; the stage is held at not_started because the text's specific process steps were not observed either way. Whether the 2025 special message qualifies as a lawful pocket rescission is a legal question not resolved here.
